goal: Stop nodes from continuing to run with corrupted database storage when reads or lookups fail
Prevent masking storage corruption as missing keys or isolated RPC failures
reviewability: Nothing known that would invalidate a review now
agreement: Unaddressed objection: aborting in reads breaks startup recovery and kills kernel hosts (furszy)
Contested objection: aborting the entire node for optional index corruption harms availability (ajtowns)
Support for removing error-catching indirection and simplifying view stack complexity (andrewtoth)
Verified by code review and local unit tests (optout21)

categories.name: indexes
why: P2 because corrupted secondary indexes previously caused silent RPC errors while the node kept running
It alters data integrity and error handling guarantees across all secondary index subsystems

categories.name: kernel
why: P2 because routing storage failures directly to fatal aborts impacts error handling in the kernel library
Host applications using the kernel depend directly on how database termination is surfaced

categories.name: validation
why: P2 because chainstate read failures previously masked storage corruption as missing keys
Ensuring disk corruption immediately stops the node protects chainstate consistency from further damage
